# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis

If you are about to make a new document and this session offers Claude's own docs (a Docs connector, docs skill or Docs artifact type), and the user has neither named Word/.docx/.dotx, asked for tracked changes, nor supplied a .docx/.dotx file to change or use as a template, make the document there instead. It exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to make a Word file. A .docx/.dotx given only as source material does not count as supplied. This skill remains the right tool for producing, reading, editing, templating or converting Word files.

A `.docx` is a ZIP archive of XML files. Choose your approach by task:

| Task | Approach |
|---|---|
| **Create** a new document | Write a `docx` (npm) script — see gotchas below |
| **Edit** an existing document | unpack → edit `word/document.xml` → `zip` (docx-js cannot open existing files) |
| **Read** content | `pandoc -t markdown file.docx` |

> Script paths below are relative to this skill's directory.

## Fitting a page limit

When a document runs over the page limit the user asked for, cut words. Don't shrink the type, narrow the margins or tighten the spacing to fit — that makes the page harder to read. Keep body text at 11–12 pt and margins at 0.75–1 in, or at the size and margins the user's own file already uses. Cut filler and repetition before facts, and cut no more than the limit needs. Safety warnings, doses, limits, fees and contract terms are an exception: keep their full meaning, with every condition attached, because readers act on them and a dropped condition can cause harm or cost money. If a document can't fit without dropping or weakening one of these items, make the margins, spacing or type slightly smaller (body text no smaller than 10 pt) or let the document run over, and tell the user which change you made and why. Then compare your version with the original and list every fact, name, number or point you removed; don't say everything was kept unless it was. If the user asks for or allows smaller type, narrower margins or tighter spacing, or says not to cut any text, do what they said.

## Creating with docx-js — gotchas

`docx` is preinstalled — do not run `npm install` first; write the script and `require('docx')` directly. Only if that require fails: `npm install docx`. The model knows the API; these are the footguns:

- **Page size defaults to A4.** For US Letter set `page: { size: { width: 12240, height: 15840 } }` (DXA; 1440 = 1″).
- **Landscape:** pass portrait dimensions and `orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE` — docx-js swaps width/height internally.
- **Tables need dual widths:** set `columnWidths` on the table AND `width` on every cell, both in `WidthType.DXA` (PERCENTAGE breaks in Google Docs). Column widths must sum to the table width.
- **Table shading:** use `ShadingType.CLEAR`, never `SOLID` (renders black).
- **Lists:** never insert `•` literally; use a `numbering` config with `LevelFormat.BULLET`.
- **`ImageRun` requires `type:`** (`"png"`, `"jpg"`, …).
- **`PageBreak` must be inside a `Paragraph`.**
- **Never use `\n`** — use separate `Paragraph` elements.
- **Headings:** style every level you use (`title`, `heading1`, `heading2`…) in `styles.default`: `heading1: { run: { font: "Arial", size: 32, bold: true }, paragraph: { spacing: { before: 240, after: 120 }, keepNext: true } }`. Every level needs its own font (even with a document default), `before` and `after` (even if 0) and `keepNext`: the built-in styles set none of them.
- **TOC:** headings must use built-in `HeadingLevel.*`; custom heading styles need `outlineLevel` set or they won't appear.
- **Don't use a table as a horizontal rule** — use a paragraph bottom border instead.
- **Dot-leader / right-aligned-on-same-line:** use `PositionalTab` (`alignment: PositionalTabAlignment.RIGHT`, `leader: PositionalTabLeader.DOT`) inside a `TextRun`, not literal `.` or space padding.

## Verify the output

After writing a `.docx`, render it and look at it:

```bash
zip -d output.docx '*/' >/dev/null || true   # drop the ZIP's folder entries: Word has refused a file that has them when opened through a cloud co-editing service
python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf output.docx
pdftoppm -jpeg -r 100 output.pdf page
ls page-*.jpg   # then Read the images
```

`pdftoppm` zero-pads page numbers to the width of the page count (`page-01.jpg`…`page-12.jpg`).

## Editing existing documents

Legacy `.doc` files must be converted first: `python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx file.doc`.

```bash
python3 -c "import sys,zipfile; zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1]).extractall('unpacked')" doc.docx   # not unzip, which restores symlinks — docx from external parties is untrusted
python scripts/merge_runs.py unpacked/   # coalesce fragmented runs so text is findable
# edit unpacked/word/document.xml in place — do NOT reformat or pretty-print
(cd unpacked && rm -f ../out.docx && zip -XrDy ../out.docx .)
python scripts/office/validate.py out.docx --original doc.docx   # XSD checks; --auto-repair fixes common issues
# redlining? add --author "<the name you redlined under>" to check every edit is tracked
```

Word splits text across many `<w:r>` runs (revision ids, spell-check markers), so a phrase you can see in the document often doesn't exist as a contiguous string in the XML. `merge_runs.py` merges adjacent identically-formatted runs in `word/document.xml` without changing content or rendering; it also accepts a `.docx` directly (`python scripts/merge_runs.py doc.docx -o merged.docx`).

**Tracked changes:** when redlining, validate with `--author "<the name you redlined under>"` (needs `--original`) — it reports any text you changed without a `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` around it, which is easy to do by accident and invisible in the accepted view. Wrap runs in `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` with `w:id`, `w:author`, `w:date` attributes. Inside `<w:del>`, the text element is `<w:delText>`, not `<w:t>`. A deleted paragraph mark (`<w:pPr><w:rPr><w:del w:id=".." w:author=".." w:date=".."/></w:rPr></w:pPr>`) means "merge this paragraph into the next" — so deleting a paragraph outright is that plus a `<w:del>` around every run. The `<w:del/>` must come before the rPr's other children; their order is schema-enforced.

To produce a clean copy with all tracked changes accepted: `python scripts/accept_changes.py in.docx out.docx`.

Accepting a deleted paragraph mark should join that paragraph to the one below it, so a paragraph whose runs are *all* deleted vanishes. Word does this; `accept_changes.py` and `pandoc --track-changes=accept` don't always. Both fail the same way — they strip the deleted text but leave the emptied paragraph behind, which reads as a stray empty bullet when it was auto-numbered:

- `pandoc --track-changes=accept` never joins the paragraphs.
- `accept_changes.py` (LibreOffice) joins them correctly, except when the deleted paragraph is followed by an empty spacer paragraph.

An empty bullet in either view is an artifact of that view, not a defect in the document. Check paragraph deletions in the XML.

## Comments

Comments require six cross-linked files. Use the helper — directory mode when you'll also be editing `document.xml` (saves an unzip/rezip cycle), `.docx`-direct mode otherwise:

```bash
# Against an already-unpacked directory (preferred when also placing markers)
python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ "Fees & expenses cap is too low"
python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ "Agreed" --parent 0

# Against a .docx directly
python scripts/comment.py contract.docx "This cap is too low" -o annotated.docx
```

The script writes `comments.xml`, `commentsExtended.xml`, `commentsIds.xml`, `commentsExtensible.xml`, the relationships, and the content-type overrides. Comment IDs are auto-assigned. It then prints the `<w:commentRangeStart>`/`<w:commentRangeEnd>`/`<w:commentReference>` snippet to add to `word/document.xml` so the comment anchors to specific text — until you place those markers, the comment exists but is not visible.

## Dependencies

`docx` (npm, preinstalled — install only if `require('docx')` fails) · `pandoc` · LibreOffice (`soffice`) · `pdftoppm` (Poppler)

once("<w:t>3: MPI Block Decomposition:</w:t>", "<w:t>3: MPI Block Decomposition</w:t>")

s = x.rfind("<w:p ", 0, part4)

assert 'w14:paraId="12677FC1"' in seg

       '<a:graphic><a:graphicData uri="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/picture">'

       'follow the order-2 reference line.</w:t></w:r></w:p>')

    return f'<w:p><w:pPr/><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">{t}</w:t></w:r></w:p>'


def h1(t):
    return f'<w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading1"/><w:keepNext/></w:pPr><w:r><w:t>{t}</w:t></w:r></w:p>'


part_head = ('<w:p><w:pPr><w:keepNext/><w:spacing w:before="360"/><w:rPr><w:b/><w:bCs/><w:sz w:val="28"/>'
             '<w:szCs w:val="36"/><w:u w:val="single"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r><w:rPr><w:b/><w:sz w:val="28"/>'
             '<w:u w:val="single"/></w:rPr><w:t>Conclusion</w:t></w:r></w:p>')
concl = [
    "We built a three-VM MPI cluster over Tailscale, verified a serial explicit solver with second-order "
    "convergence (observed orders 2.0058 to 2.0001), and parallelized it with strips and blocks. Both "
    "decompositions reproduce the serial output bit for bit, locally and across VMs.",
    "On this network a cross-VM message costs 4–7 ms and moves only 1.5–5.8 MB/s, so communication "
    "dominates every distributed run: 88–100 % of the time at N ≤ 2048 and 64–86 % at N = 8192. "
    "Distributing pays off only from about N = 8192, and only with blocks on the fastest pair: heat-2 + "
    "heat-3 took 1.11 s against 1.30 s on one VM, as the placement-aware model predicted. Where every link "
    "was measured on the same network, the model reproduced the measured times within a factor of 1.2–1.9.",
    "The network path mattered more than the decomposition. Through Tailscale’s relay on the "
    "coffee-shop network the same runs were 4–29 times slower, and the final measurements were therefore "
    "taken over direct paths on a phone hotspot.",
]
team = ("Mahmoud Hachem operated heat-2, the launch node for the benchmark campaigns. Ali Harkous operated "

cap41 = x.find("Figure 4.1. Strong-scaling speed-up")
e = x.find("</w:p>", cap41) + len("</w:p>")
x = x[:e] + part_head + "".join(body(t) for t in concl) + h1("Team contributions") + body(team) + x[e:]

doc.write_text(x, encoding="utf8")
print("ok")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Hardware and memory-bandwidth survey of every VM in a hostfile.
# Run once, from the launch VM (heat-2):
#   bash ~/part0/scripts/hardware_info.sh [HOSTFILE=~/part4/hosts_all]
# For each host it records CPU (lscpu), vCPUs, memory, GPU, and runs a
# STREAM-style memory bandwidth test (part0/src/stream.cpp) with 1 and 2 threads.
# Output: ~/part0/results/hardware/<host>.txt and summary.csv (never overwritten:
# a new run goes into a timestamped folder if results already exist).
set -uo pipefail

HOSTFILE=${1:-$HOME/part4/hosts_all}
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
SRC="$ROOT/src/stream.cpp"
OUT="$ROOT/results/hardware"
[ -e "$OUT/summary.csv" ] && OUT="$ROOT/results/hardware_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)"
mkdir -p "$OUT"
[ -f "$SRC" ] || { echo "missing $SRC" >&2; exit 1; }

HOSTS=$(awk '!/^[[:space:]]*#/ && NF {print $1}' "$HOSTFILE")
LOCAL=" $(hostname) $(hostname -I 2>/dev/null) localhost 127.0.0.1 "

# Commands run on each host; stream.cpp arrives on stdin-independent path ~/hwbench.
REMOTE='
set -u
cd ~/hwbench
echo "=== host: $(hostname)  date: $(date "+%F %T %Z")"
echo "=== lscpu"; lscpu
echo "=== nproc: $(nproc)"
echo "=== free -m"; free -m
echo "=== GPU"
if command -v lspci >/dev/null; then lspci | grep -i -E "vga|3d|display" || echo "no GPU device listed"; else echo "lspci not installed"; fi
if command -v nvidia-smi >/dev/null; then nvidia-smi -L; else echo "nvidia-smi: not present"; fi
echo "=== compiler: $(g++ --version | head -1)"
if g++ -O3 -march=native -fopenmp -o stream stream.cpp 2>/dev/null; then echo "built with OpenMP"
else g++ -O3 -march=native -o stream stream.cpp && echo "built WITHOUT OpenMP (2-thread run = 1 thread)"; fi
for t in 1 2; do echo "=== stream OMP_NUM_THREADS=$t"; OMP_NUM_THREADS=$t ./stream 20000000 10; done
'

echo "host,cpu_model,vcpus,mem_total_MB,gpu,copy_1t_GBs,triad_1t_GBs,copy_2t_GBs,triad_2t_GBs" > "$OUT/summary.csv"
for h in $HOSTS; do
    echo "--- $h"
    if [[ "$LOCAL" == *" $h "* ]]; then
        mkdir -p ~/hwbench && cp "$SRC" ~/hwbench/
        bash -c "$REMOTE" > "$OUT/tmp.txt" 2>&1
    else
        ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 "$h" 'mkdir -p ~/hwbench' &&
        scp -q -o BatchMode=yes "$SRC" "$h:hwbench/" &&
        timeout 300 ssh -o BatchMode=yes "$h" "bash -c '$REMOTE'" > "$OUT/tmp.txt" 2>&1 ||
        { echo "FAILED on $h (see $OUT/tmp.txt)"; mv "$OUT/tmp.txt" "$OUT/failed_$h.txt"; continue; }
    fi
    name=$(awk '/^=== host:/ {print $3; exit}' "$OUT/tmp.txt")
    mv "$OUT/tmp.txt" "$OUT/${name:-$h}.txt"
    f="$OUT/${name:-$h}.txt"
    model=$(awk -F: '/^Model name/ {gsub(/^[ \t]+/,"",$2); print $2; exit}' "$f" | tr ',' ';')
    vcpus=$(awk '/^=== nproc:/ {print $3}' "$f")
    mem=$(awk '/^Mem:/ {print $2; exit}' "$f")
    gpu=$(awk '/^=== GPU/ {getline; print; exit}' "$f" | tr ',' ';')
    bw() { awk -v t="$1" -v k="$2" '/^=== stream OMP_NUM_THREADS=/ {cur=substr($3,17)} cur==t && $1==k {split($2,a,"="); print a[2]}' "$f"; }
    echo "${name:-$h},$model,$vcpus,$mem,$gpu,$(bw 1 copy),$(bw 1 triad),$(bw 2 copy),$(bw 2 triad)" >> "$OUT/summary.csv"
    tail -1 "$OUT/summary.csv"
done
echo "Wrote $OUT"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Hardware and memory-bandwidth survey of every VM in a hostfile.
# Run once, from the launch VM (heat-2):
#   bash ~/part0/scripts/hardware_info.sh [HOSTFILE=~/part4/hosts_all]
# For each host it records CPU (lscpu), vCPUs, memory, GPU, and runs a
# STREAM-style memory bandwidth test (part0/src/stream.cpp) with 1 and 2 threads.
# Output: ~/part0/results/hardware/<host>.txt and summary.csv (never overwritten:
# a new run goes into a timestamped folder if results already exist).
set -uo pipefail

HOSTFILE=${1:-$HOME/part4/hosts_all}
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
SRC="$ROOT/src/stream.cpp"
OUT="$ROOT/results/hardware"
[ -e "$OUT/summary.csv" ] && OUT="$ROOT/results/hardware_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)"
mkdir -p "$OUT"
[ -f "$SRC" ] || { echo "missing $SRC" >&2; exit 1; }

HOSTS=$(awk '!/^[[:space:]]*#/ && NF {print $1}' "$HOSTFILE")
LOCAL=" $(hostname) $(hostname -I 2>/dev/null) localhost 127.0.0.1 "

# Commands run on each host; stream.cpp arrives on stdin-independent path ~/hwbench.
REMOTE='
set -u
cd ~/hwbench
echo "=== host: $(hostname)  date: $(date "+%F %T %Z")"
echo "=== lscpu"; lscpu
echo "=== nproc: $(nproc)"
echo "=== free -m"; free -m
echo "=== GPU"
if command -v lspci >/dev/null; then lspci | grep -i -E "vga|3d|display" || echo "no GPU device listed"; else echo "lspci not installed"; fi
if command -v nvidia-smi >/dev/null; then nvidia-smi -L; else echo "nvidia-smi: not present"; fi
echo "=== compiler: $(g++ --version | head -1)"
if g++ -O3 -march=native -fopenmp -o stream stream.cpp 2>/dev/null; then echo "built with OpenMP"
else g++ -O3 -march=native -o stream stream.cpp && echo "built WITHOUT OpenMP (2-thread run = 1 thread)"; fi
for t in 1 2; do echo "=== stream OMP_NUM_THREADS=$t"; OMP_NUM_THREADS=$t ./stream 20000000 10; done
'

echo "host,cpu_model,vcpus,mem_total_MB,gpu,copy_1t_GBs,triad_1t_GBs,copy_2t_GBs,triad_2t_GBs" > "$OUT/summary.csv"
for h in $HOSTS; do
    echo "--- $h"
    if [[ "$LOCAL" == *" $h "* ]]; then
        mkdir -p ~/hwbench && cp "$SRC" ~/hwbench/
        bash -c "$REMOTE" > "$OUT/tmp.txt" 2>&1
    else
        ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 "$h" 'mkdir -p ~/hwbench' &&
        scp -q -o BatchMode=yes "$SRC" "$h:hwbench/" &&
        timeout 300 ssh -o BatchMode=yes "$h" "bash -c '$REMOTE'" > "$OUT/tmp.txt" 2>&1 ||
        { echo "FAILED on $h (see $OUT/tmp.txt)"; mv "$OUT/tmp.txt" "$OUT/failed_$h.txt"; continue; }
    fi
    name=$(awk '/^=== host:/ {print $3; exit}' "$OUT/tmp.txt")
    mv "$OUT/tmp.txt" "$OUT/${name:-$h}.txt"
    f="$OUT/${name:-$h}.txt"
    model=$(awk -F: '/^Model name/ {gsub(/^[ \t]+/,"",$2); print $2; exit}' "$f" | tr ',' ';')
    vcpus=$(awk '/^=== nproc:/ {print $3}' "$f")
    mem=$(awk '/^Mem:/ {print $2; exit}' "$f")
    gpu=$(awk '/^=== GPU/ {getline; print; exit}' "$f" | tr ',' ';')
    bw() { awk -v t="$1" -v k="$2" '/^=== stream OMP_NUM_THREADS=/ {cur=substr($3,17)} cur==t && $1==k {split($2,a,"="); print a[2]}' "$f"; }
    echo "${name:-$h},$model,$vcpus,$mem,$gpu,$(bw 1 copy),$(bw 1 triad),$(bw 2 copy),$(bw 2 triad)" >> "$OUT/summary.csv"
    tail -1 "$OUT/summary.csv"
done
echo "Wrote $OUT"

    echo "${name:-$h},$model,$vcpus,$mem,$gpu,$(bw 1 copy),$(bw 1 triad),$(bw 2 copy),$(bw 2 triad)" >> "$OUT/summary.csv"
    tail -1 "$OUT/summary.csv"

I wrote the benchmark and the survey script, but neither has run on the VMs yet. Windows has no compiler, so I could only check the script's syntax and test its summary step on sample output.

**What I wrote (not committed)**
- [part0/src/stream.cpp](part0/src/stream.cpp): a memory-bandwidth test in the style of STREAM.
  - It runs the four standard operations (copy, scale, add, triad) on three arrays of 160 MB each, far larger than any cache, so it measures main memory.
  - It reports the best of 10 repetitions in GB/s, skipping the first as a warm-up.
- [part0/scripts/hardware_info.sh](part0/scripts/hardware_info.sh): you run it once from heat-2. For each VM it:
  - records the CPU model and caches (`lscpu`), the vCPU count, total memory and any GPU;
  - compiles the test on that VM and runs it with 1 and with 2 threads;
  - writes one detailed file per VM plus `summary.csv`.

  It never overwrites earlier results; a second run goes into a new timestamped folder.

**1. Copy the two files to heat-2.** In Windows PowerShell, from `C:\Users\User\Desktop\heat-mpi-project`:
```powershell
scp -P 2222 part0/src/stream.cpp mpi@127.0.0.1:~/part0/src/
```
```powershell
scp -P 2222 part0/scripts/hardware_info.sh mpi@127.0.0.1:~/part0/scripts/
```

**2. Run it on heat-2.** It takes about 1 minute; all three VMs must be on the hotspot:
```bash
bash ~/part0/scripts/hardware_info.sh ~/part4/hosts_all
cat ~/part0/results/hardware/summary.csv
```

**3. Copy the results back to Windows.** In PowerShell:
```powershell
scp -P 2222 -r mpi@127.0.0.1:~/part0/results/hardware part0/results/
```

Paste the `summary.csv` output here and I'll add a hardware table to the report for slide 1.

When you read the results:
- **CPU model:** this is the host laptop's CPU as VirtualBox passes it through. Each VM only gets 2 of its cores.
- **GPU:** this will most likely show VirtualBox's virtual display adapter (`VMware SVGA II` or `VirtualBox Graphics`). That means no compute GPU.
- **Bandwidth:** I expect a few GB/s to a few tens of GB/s per VM. That's about a thousand times the 1.5–5.8 MB/s network, which makes the slide's point for you.

import sys
from pathlib import Path

doc = Path(sys.argv[1]) / "word" / "document.xml"
x = doc.read_text(encoding="utf8")

RPR = '<w:rPr>{b}<w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="28"/></w:rPr>'


def cell(text, w, head=False):
    shd = '<w:shd w:val="clear" w:color="auto" w:fill="EBF1F4"/>' if head else '<w:vAlign w:val="center"/>'
    r = RPR.format(b="<w:b/>" if head else "")
    return (f'<w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:w="{w}" w:type="dxa"/>{shd}</w:tcPr><w:p><w:pPr>'
            f'<w:spacing w:after="0"/>{RPR.format(b="")}</w:pPr><w:r>{r}<w:t xml:space="preserve">{text}'
            f'</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:tc>')


def table(widths, rows):
    grid = "".join(f'<w:gridCol w:w="{w}"/>' for w in widths)

def table(widths, rows):

# Part 0: Three-VM MPI cluster and network measurements

This folder preserves the team's completed Part 0 code, the six sets of
ping-pong benchmark measurements, initial latency/bandwidth estimates, and
plots. It is one component of the full heat-diffusion course project.

## Cluster

- Ubuntu Server 24.04 LTS virtual machines: `heat-1`, `heat-2`, `heat-3`.
- A common Linux username: `mpi`.
- VirtualBox and Tailscale overlay networking; passwordless OpenSSH.
- Two MPI process slots per VM (see `hosts`); Open MPI 4.1.6 was used.
- Same-VM tests and cross-VM tests were carried out using MPI over TCP.
- After moving VirtualBox from NAT to Bridged Adapter, Tailscale direct
  connectivity was observed on the shared Wi-Fi; early NAT tests were relayed.

**To document before final submission:** the physical CPU model, VM RAM,
network type and `tailscale ping` direct/DERP status for **every pair**, as
well as any requested screenshots/command output. Hardware and exact network
conditions are not proven by this archive alone.

## Prerequisites

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y build-essential cmake git openmpi-bin libopenmpi-dev python3-numpy python3-matplotlib openssh-client
```

## Build

On **each** of the three Ubuntu VMs, clone/copy the repository under the
**same absolute path** and then run:

```bash
cd ~/heat-project/part0  # example path; keep the same path on all VMs
make
```

This creates `bin/hello` and `bin/pingpong` locally on each VM. Open MPI
launches the executables remotely; it does not automatically distribute them.

## Run MPI Hello World

From one VM, while in `part0`:

```bash
mpirun --hostfile hosts -np 6 \
  --mca oob_tcp_if_include tailscale0 \
  --mca btl_tcp_if_include tailscale0 \
  --mca btl tcp,self \
  "$(pwd)/bin/hello"
```

Expect two processes on each VM, six in total. The order of printed lines may
vary because processes run concurrently.

## Run a ping-pong measurement

Use exactly two processes: one on each host for cross-VM measurements, or
both on the same host for local measurements. For example:

```bash
bash scripts/run_benchmark.sh 'heat-1:1,heat-2:1' heat2_heat1_repeat.csv 10
bash scripts/run_benchmark.sh 'heat-2:2' same_heat2_repeat.csv 10
```

The helper refuses to overwrite an existing result. The benchmark sends
messages of 8, 16, ..., 16,777,216 bytes (16 MiB); each size gets 2 warm-up
round trips and 10 measured round trips (unless changed). It writes one-way
communication time as half the average round-trip time.

**Measurement detail:** `--mca btl tcp,self` forces MPI TCP communication even
for same-VM tests; local results therefore characterize MPI TCP on a single
VM, not optimized shared-memory MPI transport. On other Wi-Fi networks,
Tailscale may switch between direct and DERP relay paths.

## Analyze results

From any working directory, run:

```bash
python3 /absolute/path/to/part0/scripts/analyze_network.py
```

Or from `part0`: `python3 scripts/analyze_network.py`.

The script reads the six complete CSVs in `results/raw/`, and writes:

- `results/network_summary.csv` (latency in milliseconds, estimated effective
  bandwidth in decimal MB/s)
- `results/plots/same_vm_model.png`
- `results/plots/cross_vm_model.png`

For each pair, it estimates startup latency `t_s` as the median one-way time
for message sizes <= 1,024 bytes, and estimates transfer time per byte `t_w`
using a fixed-intercept least-squares fit for messages >= 1 MiB. The model is

3: Part 0: Building the cluster
4: We built a three-node MPI cluster using one Ubuntu Server 24.04.5 LTS virtual machine per laptop. Each VM was allocated 2 vCPUs and 4 GiB RAM in VirtualBox, uses the shared Linux account mpi, and connects to the team’s private Tailscale network. All VMs run x86_64 and Open MPI 4.1.6. SSH launches remote processes, and the MPI tests use the Tailscale interface for TCP communication.
5: heat-1: Ali Harkous / heat-2: Mahmoud Hachem/ heat-3: Amer Soulak
7: Network conditions and connectivity
8: Initially, VirtualBox NAT networking caused Tailscale to use DERP relays, producing very slow communication. For the completed cross-VM benchmarks on November 21, 2026, all three laptops shared café Wi-Fi and used VirtualBox Bridged Adapter. On November 23, 2026, all six directional Tailscale checks confirmed direct paths on shared Wi-Fi with Bridged Adapter. All six passwordless SSH directions worked, and the MPI Hello World ran six ranks across three VMs.
45: Cross-VM communication was much slower and noisier than same-VM communication; fitted values are effective estimates, not guaranteed physical link rates. The CSV data and performance graphs are archived separately. Appendices A–C contain the experiment procedure, prior DERP observations, and dated November 23 direct-route evidence. On 28 November 2026 the coffee-shop Wi-Fi used symmetric NAT (tailscale netcheck: MappingVariesByDestIP true), which forced traffic through Tailscale's Paris relay and made distributed runs stall; the final Part 3 measurements were therefore made on a phone hotspot with direct paths (tailscale ping via 172.20.10.x), measured in the last table row.
46: Part 1: Serial heat solver and verification
47: We implemented and verified a serial solver for heat diffusion on a unit square. The Case V errors decreased by a factor of about four each time the grid spacing was halved. A separate test above the stability limit produced a growing checkerboard pattern.
48: Numerical method
49: We use N intervals along each axis, so the spacing is h = 1/N and the grid contains (N + 1)² nodes. Thermal diffusivity is α = 1. At each step, the explicit five-point stencil updates an interior node from its old value and the four adjacent values.
52: Here r = Δt/h². The stable solver accepts 0 < r ≤ 0.25. For a requested final time T, it rounds the step count up and divides T by that count so the run reaches T within the requested time-step limit.
53: Cases and implementation
54: Cases 1 and 2 start with a cold interior. Case 1 holds all edges at 1. Case 2 holds the top and bottom edges, including their corners, at 1 and the remaining side nodes at 0. Case V starts from sin(πx) sin(πy) with zero edge values.
55: The C++17 solver stores each time level in a contiguous row-major array. It holds the edges fixed, updates the interior into the second array, and swaps the arrays after each step. The Makefile uses -O2 and -ffp-contract=off. We time only the step loop with std::chrono::steady_clock. The optional binary output stores the full grid as headerless little-endian doubles in row-major order.
56: Verification
57: For Cases 1 and 2, the saved checks at N = 8, r = 0.2, and 20 steps confirmed the prescribed edges and temperatures between 0 and 1.
58: For Case V, the exact solution is sin(πx) sin(πy) exp(−2π²t). At T = 0.05 with r = 0.2, the observed order of the discrete L₂ error approached 2 across N = 16, 32, 64, 128, and 256 (Appendix D). The separate instability run used r = 0.2625, 5% above the limit. The error became visible near the center of the plate and developed into a checkerboard (Appendix E). The verified serial output supplies the reference field for the MPI implementations.
59: Part 2: MPI Strip Decomposition
60: Strip ownership and halo exchange
61: The solver splits the N − 1 interior rows as evenly as possible. If the division leaves a remainder, the lowest ranks receive one extra row each. Rank 0 owns the bottom strip. Every rank stores its owned rows plus one ghost row above and one below. Appendix F shows the uneven split at N = 8 and P = 3.
62: Before each update, two MPI_Sendrecv calls exchange the first and last owned rows with adjacent ranks. Each row is already contiguous, so one message carries N + 1 doubles directly from the array. MPI_PROC_NULL handles neighbors beyond the plate. Ranks then apply the same five-point stencil as the serial solver and swap the two time-level arrays.
63: Separate blocking sends can appear to work for short rows because MPI may buffer small messages. Larger sends can wait for matching receives. If the ranks wait on one another before posting those receives, the exchange can hang. MPI_Sendrecv supplies both operations in the same call, so the matched exchanges work without relying on buffering.
64: Timing and output
65: MPI_Wtime measures halo exchange and computation separately. MPI_Reduce with MPI_MAX reports the largest rank time for each metric. The maxima can come from different ranks, so the maximum computation and communication times need not sum to the maximum total. After the timed loop, when an output file is requested (or for the Case V error check), MPI_Gatherv assembles the complete field on rank 0, which writes it in the same binary format as the serial solver. Benchmark runs skip the gather: at N = 8192 over Tailscale it moved about 268 MB and outlasted the benchmark timeout (Part 3).
66: Verification
67: The local checks covered Cases 1, 2, and V, grid sizes N = 8, 10, and 16, and P = 1 through 4. One-step Case 2 tests also checked the ghost rows at P = 2 and P = 3. Distributed Case 2 passed on two and three VMs, and a 10-step Case V run passed across three VMs. Appendix G records those results. On 28 November 2026, Case 2 also passed at P = 4 and N = 8 and 10 across heat-2 and heat-1, completing the planned C2 technical verification.
69: Part 3: MPI Block Decomposition
70: We extended the heat solver to a two-dimensional MPI block decomposition. All 72 local comparisons matched the serial binary output, including uneven partitions. On the final direct Tailscale connection between heat-2 and heat-3, blocks were faster than strips for all three grid sizes measured with four processes.
71: Block ownership and halo exchange
72: MPI_Dims_create chooses the process-grid dimensions and MPI_Cart_create builds a non-periodic Cartesian communicator. MPI_Cart_shift finds the four neighbors; physical edges have MPI_PROC_NULL neighbors. The N − 1 interior rows and columns are split as evenly as possible, with lower process coordinates receiving the remainder. Each rectangular block has one ghost layer on all four sides. Appendix H shows an uneven example.
73: Before each update, four MPI_Sendrecv calls exchange the two edge rows and two edge columns. Rows are contiguous. Columns use MPI_Type_vector with the local row stride, without manually packing a column buffer. Each rank then applies the same explicit five-point update as the serial solver, with r = Δt/h² ≤ 1/4, and swaps its two time-level arrays. Physical boundary values remain fixed.
74: Corner ghosts, timing and output
75: Corner ghosts are not exchanged because the five-point stencil reads only the center and four edge neighbors. Even a node at a block corner obtains its needed values from edge ghosts. A nine-point stencil reads diagonal neighbors and would need corner values, through diagonal messages or a second exchange extended to include the new edge ghosts.
76: MPI_Wtime measures computation and halo exchange separately. MPI_Reduce with MPI_MAX reports the largest rank time for each metric; those maxima need not come from the same rank or sum to the maximum total. Outside the timed loop, MPI_Gatherv collects packed blocks when output is requested or for the Case V error check. Rank 0 reconstructs the global field in the serial binary format.
77: Verification
78: The automated suite passed 72 of 72 comparisons for Cases 1, 2 and V; N = 8, 9, 10 and 16; and P = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8. Saved distributed comparisons also matched serial. Appendix H records the evidence. Local correctness tests may oversubscribe; the performance runs do not.

3: Part 0: Building the cluster
4: We built a three-node MPI cluster using one Ubuntu Server 24.04.5 LTS virtual machine per laptop. Each VM was allocated 2 vCPUs and 4 GiB RAM in VirtualBox, uses the shared Linux account mpi, and connects to the team’s private Tailscale network. All VMs run x86_64 and Open MPI 4.1.6. SSH launches remote processes, and the MPI tests use the Tailscale interface for TCP communication.
5: heat-1: Ali Harkous / heat-2: Mahmoud Hachem/ heat-3: Amer Soulak
7: Network conditions and connectivity
8: Initially, VirtualBox NAT networking caused Tailscale to use DERP relays, producing very slow communication. For the completed cross-VM benchmarks on November 21, 2026, all three laptops shared café Wi-Fi and used VirtualBox Bridged Adapter. On November 23, 2026, all six directional Tailscale checks confirmed direct paths on shared Wi-Fi with Bridged Adapter. All six passwordless SSH directions worked, and the MPI Hello World ran six ranks across three VMs.
45: Cross-VM communication was much slower and noisier than same-VM communication; fitted values are effective estimates, not guaranteed physical link rates. The CSV data and performance graphs are archived separately. Appendices A–C contain the experiment procedure, prior DERP observations, and dated November 23 direct-route evidence. On 28 November 2026 the coffee-shop Wi-Fi used symmetric NAT (tailscale netcheck: MappingVariesByDestIP true), which forced traffic through Tailscale's Paris relay and made distributed runs stall; the final Part 3 measurements were therefore made on a phone hotspot with direct paths (tailscale ping via 172.20.10.x), measured in the last table row.
46: Part 1: Serial heat solver and verification
47: We implemented and verified a serial solver for heat diffusion on a unit square. The Case V errors decreased by a factor of about four each time the grid spacing was halved. A separate test above the stability limit produced a growing checkerboard pattern.
48: Numerical method
49: We use N intervals along each axis, so the spacing is h = 1/N and the grid contains (N + 1)² nodes. Thermal diffusivity is α = 1. At each step, the explicit five-point stencil updates an interior node from its old value and the four adjacent values.
52: Here r = Δt/h². The stable solver accepts 0 < r ≤ 0.25. For a requested final time T, it rounds the step count up and divides T by that count so the run reaches T within the requested time-step limit.
53: Cases and implementation
54: Cases 1 and 2 start with a cold interior. Case 1 holds all edges at 1. Case 2 holds the top and bottom edges, including their corners, at 1 and the remaining side nodes at 0. Case V starts from sin(πx) sin(πy) with zero edge values.
55: The C++17 solver stores each time level in a contiguous row-major array. It holds the edges fixed, updates the interior into the second array, and swaps the arrays after each step. The Makefile uses -O2 and -ffp-contract=off. We time only the step loop with std::chrono::steady_clock. The optional binary output stores the full grid as headerless little-endian doubles in row-major order.
56: Verification
57: For Cases 1 and 2, the saved checks at N = 8, r = 0.2, and 20 steps confirmed the prescribed edges and temperatures between 0 and 1.
58: For Case V, the exact solution is sin(πx) sin(πy) exp(−2π²t). At T = 0.05 with r = 0.2, the observed order of the discrete L₂ error approached 2 across N = 16, 32, 64, 128, and 256 (Appendix D). The separate instability run used r = 0.2625, 5% above the limit. The error became visible near the center of the plate and developed into a checkerboard (Appendix E). The verified serial output supplies the reference field for the MPI implementations.
59: Part 2: MPI Strip Decomposition
60: Strip ownership and halo exchange
61: The solver splits the N − 1 interior rows as evenly as possible. If the division leaves a remainder, the lowest ranks receive one extra row each. Rank 0 owns the bottom strip. Every rank stores its owned rows plus one ghost row above and one below. Appendix F shows the uneven split at N = 8 and P = 3.
62: Before each update, two MPI_Sendrecv calls exchange the first and last owned rows with adjacent ranks. Each row is already contiguous, so one message carries N + 1 doubles directly from the array. MPI_PROC_NULL handles neighbors beyond the plate. Ranks then apply the same five-point stencil as the serial solver and swap the two time-level arrays.
63: Separate blocking sends can appear to work for short rows because MPI may buffer small messages. Larger sends can wait for matching receives. If the ranks wait on one another before posting those receives, the exchange can hang. MPI_Sendrecv supplies both operations in the same call, so the matched exchanges work without relying on buffering.
64: Timing and output
65: MPI_Wtime measures halo exchange and computation separately. MPI_Reduce with MPI_MAX reports the largest rank time for each metric. The maxima can come from different ranks, so the maximum computation and communication times need not sum to the maximum total. After the timed loop, when an output file is requested (or for the Case V error check), MPI_Gatherv assembles the complete field on rank 0, which writes it in the same binary format as the serial solver. Benchmark runs skip the gather: at N = 8192 over Tailscale it moved about 268 MB and outlasted the benchmark timeout (Part 3).
66: Verification
67: The local checks covered Cases 1, 2, and V, grid sizes N = 8, 10, and 16, and P = 1 through 4. One-step Case 2 tests also checked the ghost rows at P = 2 and P = 3. Distributed Case 2 passed on two and three VMs, and a 10-step Case V run passed across three VMs. Appendix G records those results. On 28 November 2026, Case 2 also passed at P = 4 and N = 8 and 10 across heat-2 and heat-1, completing the planned C2 technical verification.
69: Part 3: MPI Block Decomposition
70: We extended the heat solver to a two-dimensional MPI block decomposition. All 72 local comparisons matched the serial binary output, including uneven partitions. On the final direct Tailscale connection between heat-2 and heat-3, blocks were faster than strips for all three grid sizes measured with four processes.
71: Block ownership and halo exchange
72: MPI_Dims_create chooses the process-grid dimensions and MPI_Cart_create builds a non-periodic Cartesian communicator. MPI_Cart_shift finds the four neighbors; physical edges have MPI_PROC_NULL neighbors. The N − 1 interior rows and columns are split as evenly as possible, with lower process coordinates receiving the remainder. Each rectangular block has one ghost layer on all four sides. Appendix H shows an uneven example.
73: Before each update, four MPI_Sendrecv calls exchange the two edge rows and two edge columns. Rows are contiguous. Columns use MPI_Type_vector with the local row stride, without manually packing a column buffer. Each rank then applies the same explicit five-point update as the serial solver, with r = Δt/h² ≤ 1/4, and swaps its two time-level arrays. Physical boundary values remain fixed.
74: Corner ghosts, timing and output
75: Corner ghosts are not exchanged because the five-point stencil reads only the center and four edge neighbors. Even a node at a block corner obtains its needed values from edge ghosts. A nine-point stencil reads diagonal neighbors and would need corner values, through diagonal messages or a second exchange extended to include the new edge ghosts.
76: MPI_Wtime measures computation and halo exchange separately. MPI_Reduce with MPI_MAX reports the largest rank time for each metric; those maxima need not come from the same rank or sum to the maximum total. Outside the timed loop, MPI_Gatherv collects packed blocks when output is requested or for the Case V error check. Rank 0 reconstructs the global field in the serial binary format.
77: Verification
78: The automated suite passed 72 of 72 comparisons for Cases 1, 2 and V; N = 8, 9, 10 and 16; and P = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8. Saved distributed comparisons also matched serial. Appendix H records the evidence. Local correctness tests may oversubscribe; the performance runs do not.

"""Build the 1-2 page summary from the report package (same styles, page size, margins)."""
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

D = Path(sys.argv[1])  # unpacked copy of heat-mpi-REPORT.docx
docp = D / "word" / "document.xml"
x = docp.read_text(encoding="utf8")

head = x[:x.find("<w:body>") + len("<w:body>")]
sect = x[x.rfind("<w:sectPr"):x.rfind("</w:body>")]

# Convergence figure (Appendix D, rId20), scaled down.
ps = [m.group(0) for m in re.finditer(r"<w:p[ >].*?</w:p>", x, re.S)]
fig = next(ps[i - 1] for i, p in enumerate(ps) if "Figure D1" in re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", p))
assert 'r:embed="rId20"' in fig
fig = fig.replace('cx="5806440" cy="3109023"', 'cx="4180637" cy="2238497"')
fig = re.sub(r"<wp:docPr [^>]*/>", '<wp:docPr id="501" name="Picture 501"/>', fig)
fig = re.sub(r' w14:paraId="[0-9A-F]+"', "", fig)
fig = re.sub(r' w14:textId="[0-9A-F]+"', "", fig)

SZ = '<w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="24"/>'


def esc(t):
    return t.replace("&", "&").replace("<", "<").replace(">", ">")


def runs(text, bold=False):
    """Plain text with **bold**, ^{sup} and _{sub} markup."""
    out = []
    for tok in re.split(r"(\*\*.*?\*\*|\^\{.*?\}|_\{.*?\})", text):
        if not tok:
            continue
        b, va, t = bold, "", tok
        if tok.startswith("**"):
            b, t = True, tok[2:-2]
        elif tok.startswith("^{"):
            va, t = '<w:vertAlign w:val="superscript"/>', tok[2:-1]
        elif tok.startswith("_{"):
            va, t = '<w:vertAlign w:val="subscript"/>', tok[2:-1]
        out.append(f'<w:r><w:rPr>{"<w:b/>" if b else ""}{va}{SZ}</w:rPr>'
                   f'<w:t xml:space="preserve">{esc(t)}</w:t></w:r>')
    return "".join(out)


def p(text, style="Compacttext", extra=""):
    return f'<w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="{style}"/>{extra}</w:pPr>{runs(text)}</w:p>'


def bullet(text):
    return p("• " + text, extra='<w:ind w:left="284" w:hanging="200"/>')


def h(text):
    return (f'<w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading1"/><w:keepNext/><w:spacing w:before="160" w:after="60"/>'
            f'</w:pPr><w:r><w:t>{esc(text)}</w:t></w:r></w:p>')


def cell(text, w, head=False):
    shd = '<w:shd w:val="clear" w:color="auto" w:fill="EBF1F4"/>' if head else '<w:vAlign w:val="center"/>'
    return (f'<w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:w="{w}" w:type="dxa"/>{shd}</w:tcPr><w:p><w:pPr><w:spacing w:after="0"/>'
            f'<w:jc w:val="center"/></w:pPr>{runs(text, head).replace(SZ, "<w:sz w:val=\"18\"/><w:szCs w:val=\"22\"/>")}'
            '</w:p></w:tc>')


def table(widths, rows):
    grid = "".join(f'<w:gridCol w:w="{w}"/>' for w in widths)
    t = ['<w:tbl><w:tblPr><w:tblStyle w:val="TableGrid"/><w:tblW w:w="0" w:type="auto"/><w:jc w:val="center"/>'
         '<w:tblLayout w:type="fixed"/><w:tblLook w:val="04A0" w:firstRow="1" w:lastRow="0" w:firstColumn="1" '
         f'w:lastColumn="0" w:noHBand="0" w:noVBand="1"/></w:tblPr><w:tblGrid>{grid}</w:tblGrid>']
    for i, r in enumerate(rows):
        t.append('<w:tr><w:trPr><w:cantSplit/><w:jc w:val="center"/></w:trPr>'
                 + "".join(cell(c, w, i == 0) for c, w in zip(r, widths)) + "</w:tr>")
    return "".join(t) + "</w:tbl>"


body = []
body.append('<w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Title"/><w:jc w:val="center"/><w:spacing w:after="0"/><w:rPr>'
            '<w:sz w:val="40"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r><w:rPr><w:sz w:val="40"/></w:rPr><w:t>Heat MPI Project – '
            'Summary</w:t></w:r></w:p>')
body.append('<w:p><w:pPr><w:jc w:val="center"/><w:spacing w:after="120"/></w:pPr>' + runs(
    "Mahmoud Hachem (heat-2) – Ali Harkous (heat-1) – Amer Soulak (heat-3). Parallel 2D heat "
    "diffusion with MPI over Tailscale.") + "</w:p>")

body.append(h("1. Network setup"))
body += [
    bullet("**Cluster.** One Ubuntu Server 24.04.5 VM per laptop in VirtualBox, 2 vCPUs and 4 GiB each: "
           "heat-1 (AMD Ryzen 7 6800H), heat-2 (Intel i7-10510U), heat-3 (Intel i7-14700HX). Shared account "
           "mpi, passwordless SSH in all six directions, Open MPI 4.1.6, no GPU in any VM."),
    bullet("**Overlay.** Tailscale private network. MPI is pinned to it: oob_tcp_if_include and "
           "btl_tcp_if_include = tailscale0, btl = tcp,self."),
    bullet("**The path decides the speed.** VirtualBox NAT made Tailscale relay through DERP servers. "
           "Bridged mode on shared Wi-Fi gave direct paths (all six tailscale ping checks direct, 23 Nov). "
           "A coffee-shop network with symmetric NAT forced the Paris relay and distributed runs stalled, so "
           "the final measurements used a phone hotspot with direct paths (28 Nov)."),
    bullet("**Measured (MPI ping-pong, 22 sizes, t = t_{s} + m·t_{w}).** Cross-VM: t_{s} = 3.5–6.8 ms, "
           "1.5–5.8 MB/s. Same VM: t_{s} = 7–17 µs, 3.2–4.1 GB/s. Memory bandwidth (STREAM "
           "triad, 1 thread): 10.7–22.9 GB/s, three to four orders of magnitude above the network."),
]

body.append(h("2. Scientific modelling"))
body += [
    p("Heat equation u_{t} = α(u_{xx} + u_{yy}) on the unit square with α = 1 and fixed edge values. "
      "N intervals per axis, h = 1/N, (N + 1)^{2} nodes. Explicit five-point (FTCS) update:"),
    p("u_{i,j}^{n+1} = u_{i,j}^{n} + r (u_{i+1,j}^{n} + u_{i−1,j}^{n} + u_{i,j+1}^{n} + u_{i,j−1}^{n} "
      "− 4u_{i,j}^{n}),   r = Δt/h^{2} ≤ 1/4", extra='<w:jc w:val="center"/>'),
    p("Stability requires r ≤ 1/4; a run at r = 0.2625 (5 % above) grew a checkerboard error. Cases: "
      "**1** all edges at 1; **2** top and bottom at 1, sides at 0; **V** u_{0} = sin(πx) sin(πy) "
      "with zero edges, exact solution sin(πx) sin(πy) e^{−2π²t}, used to measure the error. "
      "Each step costs one update per interior point, so the compute time per step is (N − 1)^{2}·t_{c}; "
      "the stencil is memory-bound, and the measured t_{c} (1.1–3.0 ns) follows each VM’s memory "
      "bandwidth."),
]

body.append(h("3. Design choices"))
body += [
    bullet("**Serial (C++17).** Two contiguous row-major arrays swapped each step, fixed edges, -O2 "
           "-ffp-contract=off so every parallel run can be compared bit for bit with the serial binary output."),
    bullet("**Strips.** N − 1 interior rows split evenly, remainder to the lowest ranks, one ghost row per "
           "side. Two MPI_Sendrecv per step (rows are contiguous; Sendrecv avoids the deadlock of blocking "
           "sends), MPI_PROC_NULL at the plate edges."),
    bullet("**Blocks.** MPI_Dims_create + non-periodic MPI_Cart_create, MPI_Cart_shift for the four "
           "neighbours, columns sent with MPI_Type_vector (no manual packing). Corner ghosts are not exchanged: "
           "the five-point stencil never reads diagonal neighbours."),
    bullet("**Measurement.** MPI_Wtime around computation and halo exchange, MPI_Reduce(MAX) over ranks. "
           "MPI_Gatherv only for output or the Case V check, never inside benchmarks. A resumable runner "
           "keeps every failed attempt; results from different networks are never pooled."),
    bullet("**Performance model.** Per rank and step: owned points × t_{c}(VM) + Σ over real "
           "neighbours of (t_{s} + m·t_{w}) on the actual link (same VM or cross-VM); the slowest rank sets "
           "the step time."),
]

body.append(h("4. Quick results and proof of convergence"))
body.append(p("**Convergence (Case V, T = 0.05, r = 0.2).** Halving h divides the error by four: the observed "
              "order of the discrete L_{2} error is 2.0058, 2.0014, 2.0004 and 2.0001, i.e. second order in h "
              "(with Δt ∝ h^{2})."))
body.append(table([1100, 1500, 2000, 2000, 1700], [
    ["N", "Steps", "Max error", "Discrete L_{2} error", "Observed order"],
    ["16", "64", "1.66337×10^{−3}", "8.31685×10^{−4}", "—"],
    ["32", "256", "4.14182×10^{−4}", "2.07091×10^{−4}", "2.0058"],
    ["64", "1,024", "1.03442×10^{−4}", "5.17212×10^{−5}", "2.0014"],
    ["128", "4,096", "2.58542×10^{−5}", "1.29271×10^{−5}", "2.0004"],
    ["256", "16,384", "6.46314×10^{−6}", "3.23157×10^{−6}", "2.0001"],
]))
body.append(fig)
body.append(p("Figure 1. Maximum and discrete L_{2} errors against h on log–log axes; slope 2 reference.",
              "Caption"))
body += [
    bullet("**Correctness.** Strips 36/36 and blocks 72/72 local tests (Cases 1, 2, V; uneven splits; P up to 8) "
           "are bit-identical to the serial output; distributed runs on two and three VMs also match."),
    bullet("**Strips vs blocks (P = 4, heat-2 + heat-3, hotspot, 10 steps).** Blocks faster at N = 512, 2048 "
           "and 8192 by 1.08×, 1.13× and 1.48×, as the placement-aware model predicted (only the "
           "short N/2 block edge crosses the slow link); the simple interior-process model predicted strips."),
    bullet("**Scaling.** Any run leaving one VM is 88–100 % communication at N ≤ 2048 and slower than "
           "one process. Weak-scaling efficiency drops from 65–79 % inside a VM to 1–3 % across VMs."),
    bullet("**Crossover.** Predicted and measured at N = 8192: blocks on heat-2 + heat-3 took 1.11 s against "
           "1.30 s for P = 2 on one VM (communication 64–86 % of the time). The model matched measured "
           "times within 1.2–1.9× where every link was measured on the same network."),
    bullet("**Main lesson.** The network path mattered more than the decomposition: through the relay the "
           "same runs were 4–29× slower."),
]

docp.write_text(head + "".join(body) + sect + "</w:body></w:document>", encoding="utf8")

# Keep only the convergence image; drop every other media file and its relationship.
rels = D / "word" / "_rels" / "document.xml.rels"
r = rels.read_text(encoding="utf8")
keep = set()
for m in re.finditer(r'<Relationship [^>]*/>', r):
    rel = m.group(0)
    if "relationships/image" in rel and 'Id="rId20"' not in rel:
        r = r.replace(rel, "")
    elif 'Id="rId20"' in rel:
        keep.add(re.search(r'Target="media/([^"]+)"', rel).group(1))
rels.write_text(r, encoding="utf8")
for f in (D / "word" / "media").iterdir():
    if f.name not in keep:
        f.unlink()
print("ok, kept", keep)

"""Build the 1-2 page summary from the report package (same styles, page size, margins)."""
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

D = Path(sys.argv[1])  # unpacked copy of heat-mpi-REPORT.docx
docp = D / "word" / "document.xml"
x = docp.read_text(encoding="utf8")

head = x[:x.find("<w:body>") + len("<w:body>")]
sect = x[x.rfind("<w:sectPr"):x.rfind("</w:body>")]

# Convergence figure (Appendix D, rId20), scaled down.
ps = [m.group(0) for m in re.finditer(r"<w:p[ >].*?</w:p>", x, re.S)]
fig = next(ps[i - 1] for i, p in enumerate(ps) if "Figure D1" in re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", p))
assert 'r:embed="rId20"' in fig
fig = fig.replace('cx="5806440" cy="3109023"', 'cx="4180637" cy="2238497"')
fig = re.sub(r"<wp:docPr [^>]*/>", '<wp:docPr id="501" name="Picture 501"/>', fig)
fig = re.sub(r' w14:paraId="[0-9A-F]+"', "", fig)
fig = re.sub(r' w14:textId="[0-9A-F]+"', "", fig)

SZ = '<w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="24"/>'


def esc(t):
    return t.replace("&", "&").replace("<", "<").replace(">", ">")


def runs(text, bold=False):
    """Plain text with **bold**, ^{sup} and _{sub} markup."""
    out = []
    for tok in re.split(r"(\*\*.*?\*\*|\^\{.*?\}|_\{.*?\})", text):
        if not tok:
            continue
        b, va, t = bold, "", tok
        if tok.startswith("**"):
            b, t = True, tok[2:-2]
        elif tok.startswith("^{"):
            va, t = '<w:vertAlign w:val="superscript"/>', tok[2:-1]
        elif tok.startswith("_{"):
            va, t = '<w:vertAlign w:val="subscript"/>', tok[2:-1]
        out.append(f'<w:r><w:rPr>{"<w:b/>" if b else ""}{va}{SZ}</w:rPr>'
                   f'<w:t xml:space="preserve">{esc(t)}</w:t></w:r>')
    return "".join(out)


def p(text, style="Compacttext", extra=""):
    return f'<w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="{style}"/>{extra}</w:pPr>{runs(text)}</w:p>'


def bullet(text):
    return p("\u2022\u00a0" + text, extra='<w:ind w:left="284" w:hanging="200"/>')


def h(text):
    return (f'<w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Heading1"/><w:keepNext/><w:spacing w:before="160" w:after="60"/>'
            f'</w:pPr><w:r><w:t>{esc(text)}</w:t></w:r></w:p>')


def cell(text, w, head=False):
    shd = '<w:shd w:val="clear" w:color="auto" w:fill="EBF1F4"/>' if head else '<w:vAlign w:val="center"/>'
    return (f'<w:tc><w:tcPr><w:tcW w:w="{w}" w:type="dxa"/>{shd}</w:tcPr><w:p><w:pPr><w:spacing w:after="0"/>'
            f'<w:jc w:val="center"/></w:pPr>{runs(text, head).replace(SZ, "<w:sz w:val=\"18\"/><w:szCs w:val=\"22\"/>")}'
            '</w:p></w:tc>')


def table(widths, rows):
    grid = "".join(f'<w:gridCol w:w="{w}"/>' for w in widths)
    t = ['<w:tbl><w:tblPr><w:tblStyle w:val="TableGrid"/><w:tblW w:w="0" w:type="auto"/><w:jc w:val="center"/>'
         '<w:tblLayout w:type="fixed"/><w:tblLook w:val="04A0" w:firstRow="1" w:lastRow="0" w:firstColumn="1" '
         f'w:lastColumn="0" w:noHBand="0" w:noVBand="1"/></w:tblPr><w:tblGrid>{grid}</w:tblGrid>']
    for i, r in enumerate(rows):
        t.append('<w:tr><w:trPr><w:cantSplit/><w:jc w:val="center"/></w:trPr>'
                 + "".join(cell(c, w, i == 0) for c, w in zip(r, widths)) + "</w:tr>")
    return "".join(t) + "</w:tbl>"


body = []
body.append('<w:p><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Title"/><w:jc w:val="center"/><w:spacing w:after="0"/><w:rPr>'
            '<w:sz w:val="40"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r><w:rPr><w:sz w:val="40"/></w:rPr><w:t>Heat MPI Project \u2013 '
            'Summary</w:t></w:r></w:p>')
body.append('<w:p><w:pPr><w:jc w:val="center"/><w:spacing w:after="120"/></w:pPr>' + runs(
    "Mahmoud Hachem (heat-2) \u2013 Ali Harkous (heat-1) \u2013 Amer Soulak (heat-3). Parallel 2D heat "
    "diffusion with MPI over Tailscale.") + "</w:p>")

body.append(h("1. Network setup"))
body += [
    bullet("**Cluster.** One Ubuntu Server 24.04.5 VM per laptop in VirtualBox, 2 vCPUs and 4 GiB each: "
           "heat-1 (AMD Ryzen 7 6800H), heat-2 (Intel i7-10510U), heat-3 (Intel i7-14700HX). Shared account "
           "mpi, passwordless SSH in all six directions, Open MPI 4.1.6, no GPU in any VM."),
    bullet("**Overlay.** Tailscale private network. MPI is pinned to it: oob_tcp_if_include and "
           "btl_tcp_if_include = tailscale0, btl = tcp,self."),
    bullet("**The path decides the speed.** VirtualBox NAT made Tailscale relay through DERP servers. "
           "Bridged mode on shared Wi-Fi gave direct paths (all six tailscale ping checks direct, 23 Nov). "
           "A coffee-shop network with symmetric NAT forced the Paris relay and distributed runs stalled, so "
           "the final measurements used a phone hotspot with direct paths (28 Nov)."),
    bullet("**Measured (MPI ping-pong, 22 sizes, t = t_{s} + m\u00b7t_{w}).** Cross-VM: t_{s} = 3.5\u20136.8 ms, "
           "1.5\u20135.8 MB/s. Same VM: t_{s} = 7\u201317 \u00b5s, 3.2\u20134.1 GB/s. Memory bandwidth (STREAM "
           "triad, 1 thread): 10.7\u201322.9 GB/s, three to four orders of magnitude above the network."),
]

body.append(h("2. Scientific modelling"))
body += [
    p("Heat equation u_{t} = \u03b1(u_{xx} + u_{yy}) on the unit square with \u03b1 = 1 and fixed edge values. "
      "N intervals per axis, h = 1/N, (N + 1)^{2} nodes. Explicit five-point (FTCS) update:"),
    p("u_{i,j}^{n+1} = u_{i,j}^{n} + r (u_{i+1,j}^{n} + u_{i\u22121,j}^{n} + u_{i,j+1}^{n} + u_{i,j\u22121}^{n} "
      "\u2212 4u_{i,j}^{n}),   r = \u0394t/h^{2} \u2264 1/4", extra='<w:jc w:val="center"/>'),
    p("Stability requires r \u2264 1/4; a run at r = 0.2625 (5 % above) grew a checkerboard error. Cases: "
      "**1** all edges at 1; **2** top and bottom at 1, sides at 0; **V** u_{0} = sin(\u03c0x) sin(\u03c0y) "
      "with zero edges, exact solution sin(\u03c0x) sin(\u03c0y) e^{\u22122\u03c0\u00b2t}, used to measure the error. "
      "Each step costs one update per interior point, so the compute time per step is (N \u2212 1)^{2}\u00b7t_{c}; "
      "the stencil is memory-bound, and the measured t_{c} (1.1\u20133.0 ns) follows each VM\u2019s memory "
      "bandwidth."),
]

body.append(h("3. Design choices"))
body += [
    bullet("**Serial (C++17).** Two contiguous row-major arrays swapped each step, fixed edges, -O2 "
           "-ffp-contract=off so every parallel run can be compared bit for bit with the serial binary output."),
    bullet("**Strips.** N \u2212 1 interior rows split evenly, remainder to the lowest ranks, one ghost row per "
           "side. Two MPI_Sendrecv per step (rows are contiguous; Sendrecv avoids the deadlock of blocking "
           "sends), MPI_PROC_NULL at the plate edges."),
    bullet("**Blocks.** MPI_Dims_create + non-periodic MPI_Cart_create, MPI_Cart_shift for the four "
           "neighbours, columns sent with MPI_Type_vector (no manual packing). Corner ghosts are not exchanged: "
           "the five-point stencil never reads diagonal neighbours."),
    bullet("**Measurement.** MPI_Wtime around computation and halo exchange, MPI_Reduce(MAX) over ranks. "
           "MPI_Gatherv only for output or the Case V check, never inside benchmarks. A resumable runner "
           "keeps every failed attempt; results from different networks are never pooled."),
    bullet("**Performance model.** Per rank and step: owned points \u00d7 t_{c}(VM) + \u03a3 over real "
           "neighbours of (t_{s} + m\u00b7t_{w}) on the actual link (same VM or cross-VM); the slowest rank sets "
           "the step time."),
]

body.append(h("4. Quick results and proof of convergence"))
body.append(p("**Convergence (Case V, T = 0.05, r = 0.2).** Halving h divides the error by four: the observed "
              "order of the discrete L_{2} error is 2.0058, 2.0014, 2.0004 and 2.0001, i.e. second order in h "
              "(with \u0394t \u221d h^{2})."))
body.append(table([1100, 1500, 2000, 2000, 1700], [
    ["N", "Steps", "Max error", "Discrete L_{2} error", "Observed order"],
    ["16", "64", "1.66337\u00d710^{\u22123}", "8.31685\u00d710^{\u22124}", "\u2014"],
    ["32", "256", "4.14182\u00d710^{\u22124}", "2.07091\u00d710^{\u22124}", "2.0058"],
    ["64", "1,024", "1.03442\u00d710^{\u22124}", "5.17212\u00d710^{\u22125}", "2.0014"],
    ["128", "4,096", "2.58542\u00d710^{\u22125}", "1.29271\u00d710^{\u22125}", "2.0004"],
    ["256", "16,384", "6.46314\u00d710^{\u22126}", "3.23157\u00d710^{\u22126}", "2.0001"],
]))
body.append(fig)
body.append(p("Figure 1. Maximum and discrete L_{2} errors against h on log\u2013log axes; slope 2 reference.",
              "Caption"))
body += [
    bullet("**Correctness.** Strips 36/36 and blocks 72/72 local tests (Cases 1, 2, V; uneven splits; P up to 8) "
           "are bit-identical to the serial output; distributed runs on two and three VMs also match."),
    bullet("**Strips vs blocks (P = 4, heat-2 + heat-3, hotspot, 10 steps).** Blocks faster at N = 512, 2048 "
           "and 8192 by 1.08\u00d7, 1.13\u00d7 and 1.48\u00d7, as the placement-aware model predicted (only the "
           "short N/2 block edge crosses the slow link); the simple interior-process model predicted strips."),
    bullet("**Scaling.** Any run leaving one VM is 88\u2013100 % communication at N \u2264 2048 and slower than "
           "one process. Weak-scaling efficiency drops from 65\u201379 % inside a VM to 1\u20133 % across VMs."),
    bullet("**Crossover.** Predicted and measured at N = 8192: blocks on heat-2 + heat-3 took 1.11 s against "
           "1.30 s for P = 2 on one VM (communication 64\u201386 % of the time). The model matched measured "
           "times within 1.2\u20131.9\u00d7 where every link was measured on the same network."),
    bullet("**Main lesson.** The network path mattered more than the decomposition: through the relay the "
           "same runs were 4\u201329\u00d7 slower."),
]

docp.write_text(head + "".join(body) + sect + "</w:body></w:document>", encoding="utf8")

# Keep only the convergence image; drop every other media file and its relationship.
rels = D / "word" / "_rels" / "document.xml.rels"
r = rels.read_text(encoding="utf8")
keep = set()
for m in re.finditer(r'<Relationship [^>]*/>', r):
    rel = m.group(0)
    if "relationships/image" in rel and 'Id="rId20"' not in rel:
        r = r.replace(rel, "")
    elif 'Id="rId20"' in rel:
        keep.add(re.search(r'Target="media/([^"]+)"', rel).group(1))
rels.write_text(r, encoding="utf8")
for f in (D / "word" / "media").iterdir():
    if f.name not in keep:
        f.unlink()
print("ok, kept", keep)
